trial: Early versus routine oral nutritional supplementation during chemoradiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma
primary_title: Early versus routine oral nutritional supplementation during chemoradiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a randomized clinical trial
primary_results: 70/107 (65.4%) versus 88/109 (80.7%); RR 0.81 (95% CI 0.68–0.96), p=0.01; absolute reduction 15.3 percentage points; NNT 7.
secondary_results: Grade ≥3 radiation-induced oral mucositis 14.0% versus 26.6%; RR 0.53 (95% CI 0.30–0.93); p value not reported; absolute reduction 12.6 percentage points; NNT 8.
summary: Primary JAMA Oncology abstract values supersede the earlier ESMO conference analysis for numerical efficacy and safety. The ESMO report is retained for supplement dose and historical conference context.
source_note: Primary JAMA Oncology abstract (PMID 43018988) used for numerical outcomes; full article text not mined. Earlier ESMO LBA103 abstract retained only for supplement-dose and conference context.
